title: PlayBlox Hand Cricket Commentary Evaluation — Compact Prompt and Speaker Roles
note: All match facts are synthetic fixtures. Six silence cases are director-gate expectations and are not sent to Ollama.

scenarios.speaker: kabir
facts: The batter scored 4 runs on the latest delivery. No dismissal occurred.
scenarios.assignment: React casually to the result as the main commentator.
qualityChecks: Sounds like spontaneous match commentary, not a score report.
Does not force a joke.

scenarios.speaker: kabir
facts: The batter chose 3 on 6 of the last 7 deliveries.
The latest choice was also 3.
scenarios.assignment: Make a friendly roast about the repeated choice.
qualityChecks: Roast is about the repeated choice, not the player's personal traits.
Does not invent intent.

scenarios.speaker: kabir
facts: Dev just said: 'That was a brilliant tactical decision.'
The batter chose 2, and the bowler also chose 2, so the batter was dismissed.
There is no evidence the choice was tactical.
scenarios.assignment: Tease Dev's comment in a natural, friendly way.
qualityChecks: Directly responds to Dev's claim.
Funny without being hostile.
Correctly recognises the dismissal.

scenarios.speaker: kabir
facts: The batter has scored 18 runs from 9 deliveries.
The match is still in its early stages.
scenarios.assignment: Give a short general observation. Avoid turning it into a formal statistic report.
qualityChecks: Keeps the tone casual.
Does not invent a target or match situation.

scenarios.speaker: kabir
facts: The batter repeated 5 on 5 consecutive deliveries, then chose 1 on the latest delivery.
scenarios.assignment: Make a light joke about the sudden change.
qualityChecks: Joke is grounded in the sequence.
No random metaphor or invented plan.

scenarios.speaker: kabir
facts: The bowler chose 1 on 9 of their last 12 deliveries.
The batter chose 1 on 2 of their last 12 deliveries.
scenarios.assignment: Make a witty observation about the contrast between their habits.
qualityChecks: Mentions the contrast accurately.
Does not claim one player knows what the other will do.

scenarios.speaker: kabir
facts: Arjun predicted the batter would choose 6.
The batter chose 2 instead.
Arjun's prediction was wrong.
scenarios.assignment: Roast Arjun's failed prediction.
qualityChecks: Teases the prediction, not Arjun personally.
Does not claim the prediction was certain.

scenarios.speaker: kabir
facts: The latest delivery scored 1 run.
No unusual pattern, close finish or major event is present.
scenarios.assignment: Give a natural, low-key line without trying to manufacture a joke.
qualityChecks: Does not force humour or drama.
Does not add unsupported details.

scenarios.speaker: meera
facts: Across the first 10 deliveries, the batter chose 5 six times.
Across the next 10 deliveries, the batter chose 5 twice and chose 2 six times.
scenarios.assignment: Explain how the batter's choice distribution changed over time.
qualityChecks: Reports both windows correctly.
Does not infer why the player changed.

scenarios.speaker: meera
facts: In the last 20 deliveries, the batter repeated the previous choice on 13 of 19 eligible transitions (68.4%).
In the 20 deliveries before that, the repeat rate was 8 of 19 (42.1%).
scenarios.assignment: Point out the change in repeat rate, including both sample sizes.
qualityChecks: Correctly reports both rates and denominators.
Does not present the trend as permanent or causal.

scenarios.speaker: meera
facts: In 12 previous cases where this bowler chose 1 against this batter, the batter chose 2 on 8 occasions.
This is a matchup-specific sample.
scenarios.assignment: Report the conditional pattern and qualify the sample.
qualityChecks: Correctly states 8 of 12.
Makes clear it is specific to this matchup.
No prediction.

scenarios.speaker: meera
facts: Across 20 deliveries, the batter's most frequent choice appeared 6 times (30%).
The remaining 14 choices were spread across five other numbers.
scenarios.assignment: Explain why the most frequent choice is not necessarily a strong tendency.
qualityChecks: Correctly states 6 of 20 (30%).
Recognises the distribution is spread out.

scenarios.speaker: meera
facts: The batter's repeat rate is 58% across 19 eligible transitions.
The previous 19-transition window had a repeat rate of 55%.
scenarios.assignment: Explain whether this is a meaningful change.
qualityChecks: Includes the two rates and sample sizes.
Does not exaggerate a small difference.

scenarios.speaker: meera
facts: A prediction model was evaluated on 52 earlier deliveries.
It achieved 8% lower log loss than the uniform baseline and 4% lower log loss than the global baseline.
Historical performance does not guarantee the next prediction.
scenarios.assignment: Summarise the model result without overselling it.
qualityChecks: Preserves both comparisons and the 52-delivery sample.
Does not claim certainty or predictive dominance.

scenarios.speaker: dev
facts: The player's team is behind by 18 runs.
The player just scored 6 runs on the latest delivery.
scenarios.assignment: Celebrate the contribution and encourage the player.
qualityChecks: Acknowledges the score without pretending the team is winning.
Sounds warm and genuine, not like a speech.

scenarios.speaker: dev
facts: The batter was dismissed after choosing the same number as the bowler.
The batter's team is currently losing.
scenarios.assignment: Offer a supportive reaction without making fun of the player.
qualityChecks: Supportive and specific to the moment.
Does not blame or embarrass the player.

scenarios.speaker: dev
facts: The player tried a different choice after repeating 4 several times.
The new choice did not score, and the team remains behind.
scenarios.assignment: Find something encouraging about the attempt without pretending it succeeded.
qualityChecks: Recognises the attempt honestly.
Does not claim the choice was brilliant or successful.

scenarios.speaker: dev
facts: The team was 25 runs behind earlier.
It is now only 7 runs behind after a run of successful deliveries.
scenarios.assignment: Celebrate the improvement and encourage both sides to keep playing.
qualityChecks: Uses the supplied score change accurately.
Does not declare a comeback complete.

scenarios.speaker: dev
facts: One player is leading the score, while another player has not scored many runs.
Both players are still participating in the match.
scenarios.assignment: Make a supportive comment that includes both players.
qualityChecks: Does not favour only the leading player.
Does not belittle the lower-scoring player.

scenarios.speaker: dev
facts: The scores are tied.
The next delivery has not happened yet.
scenarios.assignment: Build friendly encouragement for both sides without predicting the outcome.
qualityChecks: Supports both sides equally.
Does not invent what happens next.

scenarios.speaker: arjun
facts: On the latest delivery, both batter and bowler chose 4.
Equal numeric choices dismiss the batter.
scenarios.assignment: React energetically to the dismissal.
qualityChecks: Correctly identifies the dismissal.
Uses Hand Cricket rules, not conventional cricket terms.

scenarios.speaker: arjun
facts: The batter chose Fist and the bowler chose 6.
Fist against a number scores that number; this delivery scored 6 runs.
scenarios.assignment: Call the result with energy.
qualityChecks: Correctly reports 6 runs.
Does not say the batter was dismissed.

scenarios.speaker: arjun
facts: The batter chose 2 and the bowler chose 5.
The delivery scored 2 runs; neither player was dismissed.
scenarios.assignment: Give a lively but proportionate reaction.
qualityChecks: Correctly reports 2 runs and no dismissal.
Does not exaggerate the moment.

scenarios.speaker: arjun
facts: The team was 10 runs behind before the latest delivery.
The latest delivery scored 6 runs, leaving the team 4 runs behind.
scenarios.assignment: React to the change in the match situation.
qualityChecks: Correctly describes the change.
Does not claim the team has taken the lead.

scenarios.speaker: arjun
facts: The batter chose 5 on 6 of the previous 8 deliveries.
The latest choice was 1, the first 1 in that window.
scenarios.assignment: Notice the unexpected change with energy.
qualityChecks: Mentions the change accurately.
Does not invent the reason for it.

scenarios.speaker: arjun
facts: The scores are tied with one delivery remaining.
The next delivery will decide the winner.
scenarios.assignment: Build excitement without predicting who will win.
qualityChecks: Recognises the stakes accurately.
Does not invent an outcome.

facts: The batter has made only 3 deliveries: 2, 5 and 2.
No other relevant evidence exists.
scenarios.assignment: The director should remain silent.
qualityChecks: No commentary is generated and no LLM request is made.

facts: Across 18 recent deliveries, choices are evenly spread.
No choice appears more than 3 times.
There is no notable latest event.
scenarios.assignment: The director should remain silent rather than invent a pattern.
qualityChecks: No commentary is generated and no LLM request is made.

facts: A tendency was observed 15 deliveries ago.
The last 8 deliveries do not continue that tendency.
No fresh event or insight exists.
scenarios.assignment: The director should not recycle stale evidence.
qualityChecks: No commentary is generated and no LLM request is made.

facts: A prediction model has evaluated only 8 deliveries.
No meaningful baseline comparison is available.
scenarios.assignment: The director should remain silent about model performance.
qualityChecks: No commentary is generated and no LLM request is made.

facts: The same batter tendency was discussed 2 deliveries ago.
No new evidence or meaningful change has occurred.
scenarios.assignment: The director should suppress the repeated topic.
qualityChecks: No commentary is generated and no LLM request is made.

facts: Only the latest batter choice is known: 6.
No history, score context, bowler history or outcome is supplied.
scenarios.assignment: The director should remain silent; one choice is not an insight.
qualityChecks: No commentary is generated and no LLM request is made.
